title: Lane A P3 — Step-Up Disclosure Authorization and Declassification Ledger Closure
summary: Closed the dev bypass in the review_projection CLI disclose command. Disclosure now requires mandatory single-use governance authorization receipts bound to the exact candidate bundle hash. A content-light disclosure event ledger records authorized disclosures without containing raw content, source code, or secrets. Replay is prevented through atomic consumption.

The governance disclosure authorization module (rig_relay/governance/disclosure_authorization.py) already provided a complete authority with issue/validate/consume/replay semantics. However, the review_projection CLI disclose command (rig_relay/review_projection/cli.py) had a dev bypass: the --require-authorization flag was optional and defaulted to False, allowing disclosure intent to be recorded without any step-up authorization. The governance consume_disclosure_authorization() function was unwired — nothing called it in the production disclosure path.

The _run_disclose_authorization() function now requires a mandatory authorization_id. Rather than using the generic resolve_authorization() from auth_receipts.py (which only validates), it consumes a governance disclosure receipt via consume_disclosure_authorization() with single-use semantics. The dev bypass (--require-authorization flag, WARNING output, dev_only approval) has been removed. The authorization receipt must bind to the exact candidate_zip_hash (evidence_digest), disclosure_class mapped from recipient_class, and be unexpired and unconsumed.

1. issue_disclosure_authorization() creates a receipt bound to evidence_digest (the candidate ZIP hash) and disclosure_class. 2. The CLI disclose command maps recipient_class to a governance DisclosureClass. 3. consume_disclosure_authorization() validates: receipt exists, integrity check, expiry check, consumption check, evidence_digest match. 4. On success, the receipt is atomically consumed (one_time=True, consumed=True) and re-verified after persist. 5. On any failure, a typed refusal is printed and no disclosure intent is recorded.

Path: .build/rig-relay/governance/disclosure_events.v1.jsonl. Content-light JSONL. Each record: schema_version (rig.relay.disclosure_event.v1), event_id, authorization_id, authorization_receipt_sha256, evidence_digest, disclosure_class, recipient_class, projection_id, created_at, outcome. Never contains raw source code, file contents, crosswalk values, secrets, credentials, or token-shaped values.

Replay: After consumption (one_time=True, consumed=True), second attempt returns DisclosureOutcome.ALREADY_CONSUMED → REFUSED with details
Expired: Receipt with expired expires_at returns DisclosureOutcome.EXPIRED → REFUSED
Evidence mismatch: Receipt bound to different evidence_digest returns DisclosureOutcome.EVIDENCE_MISMATCH → REFUSED
Not found: Nonexistent auth_id returns DisclosureOutcome.NOT_FOUND → REFUSED
Corrupt: Tampered receipt returns DisclosureOutcome.CORRUPT → REFUSED
Unsupported class: Invalid disclosure class returns DisclosureOutcome.UNSUPPORTED_CLASS → REFUSED

sections.content: R5 proves the disclosure event ledger contains only hashes and metadata. Forbidden content checks: source_code, raw_content, file_content, password, secret, api_key, token, ghp_/ghs_/gho_, bearer, print(, def, class. All absent. Each event has evidence_digest, authorization_id, disclosure_class, recipient_class, projection_id, outcome — content-light hashes and labels only. The review projection DisclosureAuthorizationReceipt model already has built-in safety fields: human_export_approval_required=True, controlled_disclosure_measures_recorded=True, raw_source_content_in_receipt=False.

Desktop UI for disclosure authorization — the CLI is the only executable boundary; desktop reveal UX is separate
Telemetry sharing controls — separate mission
Provider disclosure routing — separate mission
ML exports or dataset disclosure — separate mission
Browser extension disclosure — separate mission
Selective literal/comment refinement — separate mission
Crosswalk reveal (revealing pseudonym mappings) — the LocalCrosswalk model has export_prohibited=True; actual crosswalk reveal would need its own disclosure authorization class
Bundle export/transmission — the current code records intent only; actual ZIP export is a separate operation not yet implemented

None. The governance disclosure authority primitives are complete and correctly implemented. The only gap was the CLI dev bypass, now closed. The two disclosure authorization models (governance DisclosureAuthorizationReceipt and review_projection DisclosureAuthorizationReceipt) use different schemas but serve different roles: governance handles authorization lifecycle (issue/validate/consume), review_projection records intent events. This is acceptable for now but could be unified in a future schema consolidation mission.

lane_a_p3_step_up_disclosure_authority_closure_proven. The dev bypass in the review_projection CLI disclose command has been closed. A content-light disclosure event ledger records authorized disclosures without raw content. 21 tests pass. 3 static gates pass. Lane A may proceed to the next owned authority seam.
